mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic demand, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE below 4% but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment and low federal funds rate indicate economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Both UNRATE and FEDFUNDS are low but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising CPI suggests inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by 0.5% in a month
failure_condition: CPI increase but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production indicates strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate indicates tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS above 3% but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth and low unemployment indicate a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth and low unemployment but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate and rising GDP indicate economic recovery, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 60 days.
failure_condition: Low FEDFUNDS and rising GDP but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.
